verification_report.summary: The proof correctly establishes both directions. For a bipartite graph, vertices along any cycle alternate between the two bipartition classes, forcing the cycle length to be even. Conversely, shortest-path parity classes are constructed componentwise; the chosen parent edges form a spanning tree, and any edge whose endpoints have the same distance parity would combine with the unique tree path between them to form an odd cycle. All constructions and parity deductions are justified, no statement hypothesis is improperly omitted, no hard prohibition is triggered, and there are no external or internal references requiring validation.
